subject: Payment hold: clarification on April usage allocation
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan@atlasretail.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Retail Finance <invoices@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice 2027-04 - payment on hold due to usage variance

Hi Sofia,

We're reaching out from Atlas Finance — we've placed April's invoice (Invoice #2027-04-784) on hold. The billing shows a 3.7x increase in token consumption compared to our April usage budget and what we observed in staging. Our PM flagged a duplication risk tied to a burst of requests on 2027-04-22. Before we process payment, finance needs a short write-up explaining the discrepancy and the raw usage export used to calculate charges.

Please send export and a short reconciliation summary so our AP team can clear the hold.

Thanks,
Susan Park
Head of Finance Operations
Atlas Retail

Attachments: invoice-20270430.pdf
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice 2027-04 - payment on hold due to usage variance

Susan — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We see the hold on your account.

Quick summary: we observe a microburst on 2027-04-22 that tripled token counts for ~2 hours. Preliminary root cause: a client-side task retried large batched requests after a transient network timeout, which re-submitted payloads without idempotency keys. On our side, the runtime honored each request (no dedupe at ingress).

I'm sharing the usage export and a zipped set of the request trace logs where we highlight duplicated request IDs. Marissa (billing) is copying the exact CSV row slices that map to the invoice lines.

We can either: (1) propose a one-time adjustment to exclude confirmed duplicate bursts (~$4.8k) and release the payment hold, or (2) leave the invoice as-is and issue a credit on the next billing cycle after a joint audit. Which would you prefer?

I'll loop in Michael from finance for any contractual/proration considerations.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-response-logs-202704.zip
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice 2027-04 - payment on hold due to usage variance

Hi Susan — Ben here from the account team. I know this hold impacts your close schedule. Two quick points: 1) We can provisionally release the payment hold if Atlas agrees to a short joint audit window (48 hours) where we validate duplicated request IDs and confirm the rows to exclude. 2) If you need immediate short-term relief, we can apply a provisional credit equal to the disputed amount against this invoice and reconcile afterward.

If govt procurement or your AP policy requires a formal statement, we can provide: incident summary, export of the raw requests (redacted), and a reconciliation spreadsheet mapping invoice line items to request IDs. Marissa will send the spreadsheet.

Let me know which route works for you and I will flag for priority processing.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Director, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan@atlasretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice 2027-04 - payment on hold due to usage variance

Susan — attached is the raw usage export CSV (usage-export-202704.csv) and a reconciliation sheet that maps invoice rows to request_id slices. Key notes in the reconciliation:
- Rows 12,289–12,714 correspond to the burst window 2027-04-22T14:03–16:05 UTC; 94% of those rows share identical client_request_hash values, indicating retries.
- The billing engine correctly billed all accepted tokens; we don't do automatic dedupe unless idempotency_key provided.

Proposal: we can zero out the duplicated rows (estimated $4,765.20) and issue a one-time credit applied to this invoice. We'll need Atlas sign-off (email confirmation) to proceed. If you prefer an audit, we can host a short session with your engineers and ours — propose Thursday 2027-06-03 10:00 AM ET.

Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: usage-export-202704.csv, reconciliation-ATL-1392.xlsx
From: Susan Park <susan@atlasretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice 2027-04 - payment on hold due to usage variance

Marissa, Sofia, Ben — thanks for the rapid response and for the reconciliation materials.

Atlas is prepared to accept the proposed one-time credit for the duplicated burst amount (we agree the rows look like client-side retries). Please proceed to apply the $4,765.20 credit against Invoice #2027-04-784 and release the hold. Finance will process the remittance once we see the credit applied (we need an updated PDF of the invoice for our records).

Also please confirm: will Redwood update guidance on idempotency keys in the usage docs or API to reduce recurrence risk? Our engineering team would like to align on recommended best practices.

Regards,
Susan Park
Head of Finance Operations
Atlas Retail

Cc: invoices@atlasretail.com
